title: Supervisory Risk Assessment Toolkit
summary: This training programme equips supervisors with a complete, practical toolkit for assessing regulated firms: from risk-based frameworks and business model analysis to governance assessment, interviews, senior review, risk ratings and well-evidenced supervisory findings.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip supervisors to carry out a structured, evidence-based risk assessment of a regulated firm and turn it into a defensible risk rating and supervisory plan. Participants leave able to analyse a firm's business model, finances, governance and controls, test what they find through interviews and senior review, and write findings that drive action.
Intended Audience: Line supervisors and supervisory analysts responsible for assessing individual firms
Senior supervisors and team leaders who review and challenge assessments and sign off risk ratings
Risk, methodology and quality assurance staff who design or calibrate the authority's supervisory framework
sections.What It Covers: Risk-based supervisory frameworks, impact and probability, prioritisation and supervisory intensity, business model and strategy analysis, financial analysis, governance and controls assessment, supervisory interviews, thematic reviews, senior review and calibration, risk ratings and supervisory plans, and writing findings and following up.
Learning Objectives: Explain how a risk-based supervisory framework rates firms by impact and probability and sets supervisory intensity
Analyse a firm's business model, strategy and financial position to identify key vulnerabilities
Assess governance, risk management and internal controls against clear supervisory expectations
Apply structured interviewing techniques to test management's account and gather reliable evidence
Challenge and calibrate risk assessments through thematic reviews and senior review
Translate assessments into risk ratings, supervisory plans and clearly written findings that are followed through
sections.Modules Intro: Ten modules that follow the supervisory assessment cycle from framework to findings, with a running case study and practical exercises throughout.
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines short input with case studies, group exercises and practical tools, building to an end-to-end assessment workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's own framework.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising regulated firms is helpful. No specialist financial or analytical background is required.
sections.Materials: Course notes for all 10 modules. Case-study firm pack, business model analysis template, interview planning guide and review pack template. Attendance certificate stating the teaching hours completed; CPD recognition depends on each participant's professional body.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision (2024)
IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)

modules.title: Risk-Based Supervision: Principles and Frameworks
modules.summary: The logic of risk-based supervision, how authorities combine the impact of a firm's failure with the probability of it happening, and how the framework structures every later assessment.
objectives: Explain why risk-based supervision replaced compliance-based approaches
Distinguish impact and probability and how each is assessed
Map the risk categories and elements of the authority's supervisory risk framework
syllabus: From compliance checking to risk-based and outcomes-based supervision
Impact: size, systemic importance, customer reach and substitutability
Probability: inherent risks, controls, governance and financial resilience
International principles on risk-based supervision across sectors

modules.title: Prioritisation, Supervisory Intensity and Resource Allocation
modules.summary: How an authority sets its own risk appetite, varies supervisory intensity across the regulated population and makes explicit, defensible trade-offs when resources are limited.
objectives: Apply a supervisory risk appetite to prioritise firms and issues
Assess intensity models and the trade-off between breadth and depth
Formulate a risk-based work plan that can be reprioritised as risks change
syllabus: The authority's risk appetite and tolerance for firm failure
Supervisory intensity tiers and minimum engagement models
Allocating scarce resource and explaining the trade-offs
Exercise: reprioritising a work plan mid-year

modules.title: Business Model and Strategy Analysis
modules.summary: Why supervisors analyse business models and strategy, how a firm creates and sustains value, and a practical roadmap for scoping a proportionate business model analysis.
objectives: Explain what a business model and corporate strategy are and why they matter to supervisors
Identify the facets of business model and strategy risk
Plan a proportionate business model analysis using appropriate information sources
syllabus: Firm characterisation: products, customers, channels and value chain
Where strategy and business model risk sit in the risk framework
Assessing the business environment: competition, buyer and supplier power, new entrants
Roadmap, proportionality and the preliminary assessment

modules.title: Financial Analysis for Supervisors
modules.summary: The quantitative side of risk assessment: reading a firm's financial position, testing the sustainability of earnings and capital, and challenging projections and the assumptions behind them.
objectives: Analyse profitability, capital and liquidity indicators to identify vulnerabilities
Assess concentration and dependency risks in earnings and funding
Challenge financial projections and the execution risk behind a strategy
syllabus: Profitability key risk indicators and drivers of earnings
Capital structure, capital quality and liquidity buffers
Concentration, dependency and peer comparison
Why strategies fail: projections, assumptions and execution risk

modules.title: Assessing Governance Risk
modules.summary: What governance risk is, how supervisors assess board effectiveness, accountability and culture, and how to reach a well-supported conclusion on the quality of a firm's governance.
objectives: Describe the sub-categories of governance risk
Plan and carry out a governance assessment using documents, observation and interviews
Draw and evidence conclusions on governance effectiveness
syllabus: Governance risk: board, management, accountability, culture and group influence
Evidence sources: board packs, minutes, evaluations and committee papers
Red flags: dominant individuals, weak challenge and unclear accountability
Rating governance and linking it to other risk categories

modules.title: Assessing Risk Management and Internal Controls
modules.summary: How supervisors judge whether a firm's risk management framework and control functions actually work, rather than merely exist, and how control quality affects the overall risk rating.
objectives: Evaluate the design and operation of the risk management framework
Assess the independence, resourcing and influence of the control functions
Judge whether controls adequately mitigate the inherent risks identified
syllabus: Risk appetite, risk identification and management information
Risk, compliance and internal audit: independence, stature and coverage
Testing controls: walk-throughs, sample testing and outcomes evidence
Net risk: weighing controls against inherent risk

modules.title: Supervisory Interviews and Evidence Gathering
modules.summary: How to plan and conduct interviews with directors and senior managers, test the credibility of what is said, handle evasive or defensive interviewees and record reliable evidence.
objectives: Plan interviews with clear objectives and an evidence-led question strategy
Apply questioning techniques and recognise evasion and inconsistency
Link interview evidence to supervisory conclusions and action
syllabus: Interview planning, roles and the supervisory mindset
Open, probing and closed questions; funnelling and challenge
Credibility, consistency and handling difficult interviewees
Recording interviews and corroborating with documentary evidence

modules.title: Thematic Reviews and Cross-Firm Analysis
modules.summary: When and how to use thematic reviews to examine a risk across many firms, how to scope them tightly, and how to use the results in both firm-level and sector-wide supervision.
objectives: Explain what drives a thematic review and the main types of review
Design a tightly scoped review that avoids over-reach
Use thematic findings to inform firm ratings, policy and industry communication
syllabus: Triggers for thematic work: emerging risks, outliers and policy questions
Scoping, sampling and avoiding the over-scoped 'Christmas tree' review
Managing moral hazard and expectations created by thematic findings
Thematic governance: review, sign-off and reporting of findings

modules.title: Senior Review and Calibrating Risk Ratings
modules.summary: How senior review challenges and calibrates supervisory assessments, who presents, reviews and signs off, and how to prepare a review pack that supports a consistent, defensible rating.
objectives: Describe where senior review sits in the supervisory architecture and how it operates
Prepare a review pack with a clear supervisory narrative and assessment of materiality
Contribute to open, constructive challenge as presenter or reviewer
syllabus: Before, during and after review: preparation, discussion and agreed actions
Roles of presenter, chair, reviewers and secretary, and escalation to formal decisions
The review pack: narrative, evidence, materiality and proposed rating
Consistency of ratings across firms and over time

modules.title: From Assessment to Action: Findings, Plans and Follow-Up
modules.summary: Brings the toolkit together: choosing proportionate supervisory tools, writing findings that firms understand and act on, setting a supervisory plan and tracking remediation to closure.
objectives: Select proportionate supervisory tools and interventions for the risks identified
Write clear, evidenced findings and a risk mitigation programme
Track remediation and decide when to close or escalate
syllabus: The supervisory toolkit: from letters to formal requirements
Writing findings: issue, evidence, risk, required action and deadline
Supervisory plans, follow-up and validating remediation
Workshop: end-to-end risk assessment of a case-study firm

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.

related.title: Core Supervisory Skills: Business Models, Governance and Supervisory Architecture
related.summary: A three-day workshop taking supervisors from business model analysis through governance interviews to senior review of their assessment, using running case studies and role plays.

related.title: Supervisory Judgement and Professional Practice
related.summary: A ten-module programme on forming, documenting and defending supervisory judgements, and turning them into clear findings, letters and interventions.

related.title: Investigative and Interviewing Skills for Supervisors
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme on planning and conducting supervisory interviews and turning interview evidence into sound findings.

related.title: Authorisation and Licensing: The Regulatory Gateway
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving authorisation staff a structured, defensible methodology for assessing applications, key individuals, owners and changes at the regulatory gateway.

related.title: Fit and Proper Assessments: Approving Owners, Directors and Key Function Holders
related.summary: An eight-module practitioner programme on assessing owners, controllers, directors and key function holders, from evidence gathering and interviews to defensible decisions.
